hero.title: Release once. Every host picks it up.
hero.lead: Lode Server keeps the releases of your software and hands them to lode, the small loader that verifies, starts and updates an app on each host. You publish a version; the hosts do the rest.

stack.caption: A package in the registry. Hosts that follow stable run 1.4.2 until you publish the next one.

packages.title: A namespace of your own
packages.body: Each account gets a namespace. Put packages in it, public or private, each with its own channels — stable, beta, or whatever you name them.

signed.title: Signatures a host can check
signed.body: Sign files with your key. The registry never sees a private key, and a host that pins your public key refuses anything signed by someone else.

ci.title: One step in your pipeline
ci.body: A single command uploads the build output, up to 500 MiB a file, and publishes the version in one move. No host ever sees half a release.

tokens.title: Tokens that reach one package
tokens.body: Let a pipeline write to one package, or a host read a private one. A token that leaks opens nothing else.

steps.title: How it works
steps.lead: Three things happen, and only the first one is yours to do by hand.

create.title: Create a package
create.body: Sign in, name the package, and make a token that may write to it.

publish.title: Publish from CI
publish.body: Your pipeline uploads the files and publishes the version to a channel.

run.title: Hosts update themselves
run.body: lode on each host checks the channel, verifies the download, switches over, and rolls back if the new version does not start.

publish.title: Publish a release
publish.lead: Set up once; after that the pipeline does it on every release.

package.title: Create a package
package.body: In the console, create a package and choose whether it is public or private. Its address is your namespace and its slug: <namespace>/<slug>.

token.title: Create a token
token.body: On the Access tokens page, make a token with a write grant on this package only. Save it as the pipeline secret LODE_REGISTRY_TOKEN — it is shown once.

key.title: Optional: sign your releases
key.body: Generate a key pair once. Keep the seed as the secret LODE_SIGNING_KEY and give the trusted_keys line it prints to whoever runs your software. The publish command registers the public key for you.

publish.title: Publish
publish.body: The command opens a draft, uploads each file under its own name, then publishes to the channel. Hosts pick a file by name, so name files after the platform. Leave out --key-env to publish unsigned.

ci.title: Put it in the pipeline
ci.body: The same command as a workflow step. A complete GitHub Actions workflow, including how to get lode-cli onto the runner, is in examples/publish of the lode-server repository.

notes.rerun: If a run fails, start it again: it continues into the draft it left.
notes.size: Files up to 95 MiB go in one request, larger ones in parts. The limit is 500 MiB a file.
notes.immutable: A published version cannot be changed. Publish a new one, or point the channel back at an earlier one.

install.title: Install with lode
install.lead: What goes on a host to run a package from here and keep it current.

config.title: Point lode at the package
config.body: The manifest address is on the package's Install tab. The asset is the exact file this host should install.

trust.title: Pin the publisher's key
trust.body: Get the trusted_keys line from the publisher and enforce signatures. The host then installs only what that key signed, whatever the registry serves.

private.title: For a private package
private.body: Add a token with a read grant on the package. Pass it in the environment; lode sends it to the registry and nowhere else.

run.title: Run it
run.body: lode downloads the current version, verifies it, starts it, and keeps watching the channel.

notes.rollback: lode will not follow a channel back to an older version by itself. To downgrade on purpose, use lode-cli rollback or pin a version.
notes.unsigned: Without trusted_keys, an unsigned package is installed on the registry's word alone. Sign anything that matters.
notes.rate: Requests are limited per client address. Hosts behind one address share the allowance.

closing.title: Start with one package
closing.body: Create it in the console, publish a first version, and point a host at it.

footer.tagline: Lode Server, a release registry for lode.

download.title: Get lode
download.lead: One download serves both sides. Hosts run lode; publishers use lode-cli, the same binary under another name.

binary.title: As a binary
binary.body: A static build for Linux and macOS. Each archive holds lode and lode-cli; once installed, lode-cli self-update moves to a newer release.

image.title: In a container image
image.body: The image carries only the binary. Copy it into the image your app already uses.

download.note: Releases are signed. The archives come with .sig files and a SHA256SUMS list on the release page.
